text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Private mobile phone operator Telecel is worth between 135 and 160 billion escudos, according to analysts. Telepri- Telecomunicacoes Privadas SGPS SA is considering an initial public offering of shares in Telecel Comunicacoes Pessoais SA.

- Banco Espirito Santo (BES) is preparing to issue 25 billion escudos of subordinated debt to reinforce its capital in order to bid for Banco Internacional de Credito (BIC) and Banco Essi, a source familiar with the process told the paper.
- Car retailer Salvador Caetano SA registered sales of 28.8 billion escudos in the first half of 1996, 1.7 billion escudos above the same period of 1995.
- The Portuguese want to see 1997 budget approved even if it means a rise in taxes next year, an opinion poll showed.
- Requests for Cimpor shares in the second stage privatisation of the cement group exceeded Portugal Telecom at a similar stage of the pre-registration period.
- The last IMF, EU and OECD forecasts place Portugal in the group which will join the European single currency in 1999.

- Women suffer greatly in unemployment statistics. Unemployment among women grew by 4.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996, compared to the same period of 1995, according to National Statistics Institute. Unemployment among men eased by 0.2 percent in the same period.
